sub: In early 1789, Nguyễn Huệ's forces routed a Qing army near Thăng Long. Then he asked the Qing for recognition.
say: In early seventeen eighty-nine, Nwin Hweh's forces routed a Ching army near Tahng Long. Then he asked the Ching for recognition.

title: TÂY SƠN
sub: In 1771, three brothers, Nguyễn Nhạc, Nguyễn Huệ and Nguyễn Lữ, began an uprising in Tây Sơn, in what is now Bình Định province.
say: In seventeen seventy-one, three brothers, Nwin Nyahk, Nwin Hweh and Nwin Loo, began an uprising in Tay Sun, in what is now Bin Din province.

title: A DIVIDED LAND
sub: The Trịnh controlled the north and the Nguyễn the south, while the Lê emperor's authority was largely nominal. In 1786, Tây Sơn forces entered Thăng Long.
say: The Chin controlled the north and the Nwin the south, while the Lay emperor's authority was largely nominal. In seventeen eighty-six, Tay Sun forces entered Tahng Long.

title: THE QING ARRIVE
sub: The Lê ruler Lê Chiêu Thống fled to China and sought Qing help. In late 1788, Qing forces entered Vietnam and captured Thăng Long.
say: The Lay ruler Lay Chew Tong fled to China and sought Ching help. In late seventeen eighty-eight, Ching forces entered Vietnam and captured Tahng Long.

title: QUANG TRUNG
sub: In late 1788, Nguyễn Huệ proclaimed himself emperor, as Quang Trung, and marched north.
say: In late seventeen eighty-eight, Nwin Hweh proclaimed himself emperor, as Kwahng Chung, and marched north.

title: TẾT ATTACK
sub: Around Lunar New Year in 1789, Quang Trung's forces attacked Qing positions near Thăng Long, and the Qing army retreated north.
say: Around Lunar New Year in seventeen eighty-nine, Kwahng Chung's forces attacked Ching positions near Tahng Long, and the Ching army retreated north.

title: HOW MANY?
sub: How many soldiers? Estimates vary. Qing records give about twenty thousand. Vietnamese accounts report far higher figures.
say: How many soldiers? Estimates vary. Ching records give about twenty thousand. Vietnamese accounts report far higher figures.

title: THE STAND-IN
sub: After the battle, Quang Trung sought Qing recognition. The Qing recognized him as King of Annam, and asked him to visit Beijing for the emperor's eightieth birthday. Some later accounts say a stand-in went. Historians dispute that story.
say: After the battle, Kwahng Chung sought Ching recognition. The Ching recognized him as King of Ah-nahm, and asked him to visit Beijing for the emperor's eightieth birthday. Some later accounts say a stand-in went. Historians dispute that story.

title: TWO VIEWS
sub: Vietnamese accounts celebrate the battle as a major victory. Yet the Annam campaign was also counted among the Qianlong emperor's Ten Great Campaigns.
say: Vietnamese accounts celebrate the battle as a major victory. Yet the Ah-nahm campaign was also counted among the Chyen-long emperor's Ten Great Campaigns.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: Win the battle. Then make the peace look like a win for everyone. Follow for more.
say: Win the battle. Then make the peace look like a win for everyone. Follow for more.
